strengths: Well-motivated hybrid architecture combining GNNs for local topology with Transformers for global dependencies, directly addressing MWPM's limitations in exploiting syndrome information

Parameter-efficient design maintaining ~3.9M parameters across all tested code sizes while competing method (QECCT) scales to 6.71M
Clear presentation with well-structured background material and informative visualizations of the decoding pipeline and learning dynamics
Sound technical framework with principled graph construction, feature engineering, and weight conversion via negative log-likelihood

Severe reproducibility gaps including no code availability, incomplete ground truth algorithm specification, absent error bars/confidence intervals on all results, and missing ablation studies on architectural choices (why max vs. mean/min for edge aggregation in Eq. 24?)

Limited novelty: hybrid ML+classical QEC approaches and GNN+Transformer combinations already exist; main contribution is engineering-focused combination of known components without conceptual advances

Incomplete experimental analysis: improvements are modest at smaller lattice sizes (L=6,8), threshold estimates rely on limited data points (4-5 per figure) making precision claims questionable, and no statistical significance testing

Quadratic computational complexity O(E²d²) due to Transformer encoder not analyzed for scalability; no runtime comparisons with baselines and unclear applicability to real quantum systems with millions of qubits

Missing critical experimental details: train/test data split unspecified, no validation that weight distribution (Figure 5) corresponds to correct vs. incorrect edges, no mechanistic explanation for larger improvements under depolarizing noise, and hyperparameter selection (λ=0.01) appears arbitrary

Parameter-efficient architecture maintaining ~3.9M parameters across code sizes compared to 6.71M for QECCT
Clear presentation of the hybrid GNN+Transformer architecture with detailed mathematical formulation

Marginal improvements over state-of-the-art: paper acknowledges 'modest improvements' over QECCT at smaller lattice sizes (L=6,8) and only marginal gains at L=5,7 for Rotated Surface Code

Ground truth generation methodology is problematic: uses heuristic clustering with fallback to 'timed brute-force search' (unspecified), no analysis of failure rates or bias this introduces to training supervision
Critical evaluation gaps: no error bars or confidence intervals on any curves (Figures 2-4), no statistical significance testing, test set sizes unspecified, variance across runs unknown

Ground truth generation severely under-specified: Algorithm 2 lacks details on clustering procedure and permutation search; potential for training on corrupted labels undermines results
Only tested on small codes (L≤10) with unknown scalability to fault-tolerant regime (L≥100); generalization across different noise models not demonstrated
No comparison with other recent GNN-based decoders (Lange et al. 2025) or thorough engagement with tensor-network/union-find methods; baseline selection appears selective

Well-motivated hybrid GNN+Transformer architecture that properly decomposes the problem: local topological feature extraction via GNN followed by global dependency modeling via Transformer

Strong experimental results with substantial LER improvements (17-50% reduction at L=10 on depolarizing noise) and superior thresholds (10.95% vs 10.3% for independent noise, 17.9% vs 16.0% for depolarizing)
Parameter efficiency advantage: maintains ~3.9M parameters across all code sizes while QECCT reaches 6.71M at L=10, important for practical scalability
Comprehensive experimental validation across two code families (Toric, Rotated Surface), two noise models (independent, depolarizing), and multiple baselines including state-of-the-art QECCT
Insightful model analysis demonstrating learning dynamics through weight distribution evolution (Figure 5), showing sharp polarization indicating successful learning
Detailed hyperparameter specification and training procedures facilitate reproducibility within reasonable constraints
weaknesses: Limited code size testing (L ≤ 10 for Toric, L ≤ 7 for Rotated Surface) raises critical questions about practical scalability for fault-tolerant quantum computing which requires L ~ 1000+; no evidence that training generalizes across code sizes

Computational complexity analysis underemphasizes O(E²d_hidden) scaling in Transformer stage; no wall-clock time comparisons, inference latency measurements, or demonstrated feasibility for real-time quantum processor feedback

Insufficient ablation studies: no validation of architecture necessity (why Transformer + GNN over pure Transformer?), edge aggregation choice (Eq. 24 max operator unjustified), or hyperparameter sensitivity beyond λ

strengths: Sound technical approach to a hard problem: Creative proxy loss formulation (BCE + entropy regularization) effectively addresses MWPM's non-differentiability, enabling end-to-end neural augmentation of a classical algorithm

Strong experimental results on depolarizing noise: Achieves thresholds of 17.9% (toric) and 17.7% (rotated surface) very close to maximum likelihood bounds (18.9% and 18.0%), outperforming QECCT and classical baselines

Excellent generalization properties: Demonstrates robust interpolation within training distribution, extrapolation to unseen error rates (p=0.03, p=0.23), and successful transfer learning across code distances
Practical efficiency advantages: Maintains constant parameter count (~3.9M) across code distances versus QECCT's quadratic growth (6.64M at L=10); achieves faster inference (4.01ms vs 20.1ms at L=10)

Well-motivated hybrid architecture: GNN for local syndrome topology extraction followed by Transformer for global error chain correlations is intuitive and validated by ablation showing Transformers are essential

Comprehensive experimental coverage: Multiple codes (toric, rotated surface, repetition), noise models (independent, depolarizing, circuit-level), and distances tested with clear presentation and extensive appendices
Thoughtful implementation: Ground truth generation handles degeneracy through deterministic heuristic; virtual node augmentation for boundary conditions; detailed reproducibility information
weaknesses: Critical gap in ground truth analysis: Relies on heuristic clustering algorithm for training labels but provides no systematic analysis of label quality, fraction matching optimal solutions, or potential systematic bias. Label purity is crucial for supervised learning but remains unvalidated

Inconsistent improvements over recent baselines: Strong gains on toric code under depolarizing noise, but marginal improvements on rotated surface code (Figures 2f-g) where NMWPM and QECCT curves nearly overlap. Unclear if advantages are code-specific rather than fundamental

Limited practical noise model validation: Only synthetic depolarizing and independent noise tested thoroughly. Circuit-level noise only evaluated on tiny codes (L≤5, Figure 3). No correlated, biased, or fabrication-realistic noise from specific quantum platforms. Applicability to real hardware unclear

Unaddressed scalability to practical regime: Largest experiments use L=12 (toric) and L=9 (rotated surface), far below fault-tolerant requirements (L~100-1000). Transformer encoder's O(E²) complexity will scale poorly. No discussion of practical scalability

Unclear training and evaluation protocol: Paper does not clearly specify whether models train jointly on all code distances or separately per distance. Cross-distance training methodology and validation set selection are unexplained, complicating reproducibility and generalization claims

Loss function lacks rigorous justification: Why is BCE on edge probabilities the right proxy for optimizing MWPM matching quality? Connection between minimizing prediction loss and matching performance is empirical rather than theoretically grounded. Entropy regularization helps but is not justified

Modest algorithmic novelty: Hybrid neural-classical decoders are established (QECCT, Bausch et al. 2024). Contribution is primarily engineering (GNN + Transformer combination); proxy loss uses standard ML techniques (BCE + entropy reg). Incremental rather than novel methodology

Missing statistical rigor: Figures lack confidence intervals or error bars; unclear if single run or averaged across seeds. Threshold estimation methodology undefined. No sensitivity analysis for hyperparameters (λ=0.01, learning rate schedule)

Incomplete ablation studies: Figure 4b ablates some components but not GNN depth, Transformer depth, hidden dimension, attention heads, or architectural ordering. Edge aggregation strategy (max vs. mean vs. min) not thoroughly explored

Reproducibility constraints: Heavy dependence on external PyMatching library; complex ground truth generation with multiple fallbacks; large GPU requirements (48GB L40); code not yet available (2026 repository)

strengths: Sound hybrid architecture elegantly preserving MWPM structure while augmenting with learned weights; GNN+Transformer combination reasonably captures local and global dependencies

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple codes (Toric, Rotated Surface, Repetition), noise models (independent, depolarizing, circuit-level), and baselines (MWPM, QECCT, BPOSD-2) with proper threshold analysis
Strong parameter efficiency (3.9M params vs QECCT's 6.7M at L=10) and 2-5× faster inference times (4.01ms vs 20.1ms at L=10), demonstrating practical advantages
Thorough supplementary material with reproducibility details, ablation studies, transfer learning experiments, and architectural specifications
Reasonable treatment of code degeneracy via clustering-based ground truth generation with sensible fallback mechanisms
weaknesses: Marginal empirical improvements over QECCT: 17.9% vs 17.8% (Toric depolarizing), 10.95% vs 10.7% (independent), and 17.7% vs 17.2% (Rotated)—differences within experimental noise margins, undermining claims of 'superior scaling'

Fundamental unresolved train-test mismatch: BCE loss during training does not enforce perfect matching constraint (every vertex matched exactly once); constraint is only imposed post-hoc by MWPM at inference. This significant divergence between optimization objective and inference requirement is acknowledged but not adequately analyzed or addressed

Ground truth generation via heuristic clustering may systematically deviate from optimal MWPM solutions, raising critical question of what the network actually learns: genuine improvements or fitting to suboptimal heuristic labels? Paper acknowledges but insufficiently addresses this

Limited conceptual novelty: hybrid neural-classical QEC approaches are well-established; GNNs and Transformers are standard; core contribution (edge weight prediction) is incremental engineering combination of existing ideas. Recent concurrent work (Bausch et al. 2024, Senior et al. 2025) pursues similar strategies

Weak generalization evidence: interpolation only within training range [0.05, 0.20]; extrapolation tested at only 2 points; transfer learning shown for single code distance change with modest gains; no cross-code generalization (Toric→Rotated) demonstrated
Limited circuit-level noise evaluation: only tiny codes tested (L=3,5 for repetition code), despite circuit-level noise being the critical bottleneck for practical quantum computing

Incomplete architectural justification: limited ablation on TransformerConv choice; no GNN-only or Transformer-only comparisons; depth/width sensitivity not explored; edge probability aggregation (max vs min) justified only post-hoc

strengths: Well-motivated hybrid approach combining neural networks with classical MWPM; creative proxy loss formulation enabling differentiation through non-differentiable algorithm
Thoughtful two-stage architecture (GNN for local topology + Transformer for global dependencies) well-suited to syndrome graph structure
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple codes, noise models, and code distances with diverse baselines and strong threshold results (17.9% vs 18.9% ML bound)
Excellent empirical analysis: weight distribution evolution, generalization across error rates and code topologies, transfer learning capabilities, and ablation studies validate design choices
Practical efficiency advantage: maintains ~3.9M parameters across all code sizes vs QECCT's 6.71M; faster inference than QECCT (2.47ms vs 7.00ms at L=6)

weaknesses: Ground truth generation heuristic (Algorithm 2) is complex and raises concerns: ~0.2% data discarded due to timeout; labels deliberately deviate from classical MWPM solutions; unclear whether network learns optimal corrections or mimics heuristic; no validation that non-trivial labels actually improve decoding
